title: The two-point decision
summary: Kick for 1 or run a play for 2, and how the score tells a coach which one to pick.

steps.text: After a touchdown a team gets one bonus try. The easy choice is the extra point: kick it through the goal posts for 1 point. Kickers make almost every one, so it is close to a sure thing.

The other choice is to go for 2. The offense lines up at the 2-yard line and runs one regular play. Get the ball into the end zone and it is worth 2 points. Fail and you get nothing. It works less than half the time.
Here the quarterback throws a quick slant. The receiver takes one step upfield and cuts inside. From the 2-yard line there is no time for a long route, so 2-point plays are fast and simple.

So when do teams take the gamble? When the score says they need it. Say you are down by 8 late in the game. A touchdown makes it a 2-point gap. Kicking the extra point leaves you down 1, and the game could end that way. Going for 2 and making it ties the game.

Coaches count in sevens and threes. Down by 14? Two touchdowns with two kicks ties it, so kick. Down by 15? Two touchdowns and two kicks leaves you 1 short, so at some point you need a 2. The rule is simple: if the sure 1 point is enough, kick. If it is not, go for 2.

quiz.prompt: Where does the offense line up for a 2-point try?
quiz.explanation: One play from the 2-yard line. Score and it is worth 2 points.

quiz.prompt: Tap the quarterback who throws the quick slant on this 2-point play.
quiz.explanation: From the 2-yard line there is no time. The quarterback takes the snap and fires the slant right away.

quiz.prompt: Your team is down by 8 late in the game and just scored a touchdown. Now you are down by 2. What should you do?
choices: Kick the extra point to get within 1
Go for 2 to tie the game
quiz.explanation: Down by 2, the kick only gets you to 1 behind. Only a 2-point try can tie it.

quiz.prompt: Your team scores a touchdown early in the game and now leads by 6. What should you usually do?
quiz.explanation: Early in the game, take the near-sure point. Save the gamble for when the score says you need it.

quiz.prompt: Why is the extra point kick the usual choice?
choices: Kickers make almost all of them, so it is nearly sure
quiz.explanation: One nearly-sure point beats a 2-point try that fails more often than it works, unless you need the 2.
